newsitem.title: USA: Oscar Mayer relishes Super Bowl sponsorship.
newsitem.headline: Oscar Mayer relishes Super Bowl sponsorship.

text.p: For meat marketer Oscar Mayer, a Super Bowl featuring a home state team -- Wisconsin's Green Bay Packers -- is an incredible stroke of luck.
"We could not have scripted it any better," said Mark Zander, category business director for the Madison, Wis.-based unit of Philip Morris' Kraft Foods Inc.
"Overall, this place is pretty excited about being in the Super Bowl. A lot of us were born and raised Packer fans, and this is unbelievable," Zander said.
Oscar Mayer, the sole sponsor of Super Bowl XXXI's half-time show on Jan. 26, will use the game as a platform to showcase winners of its national talent search contest.
In the 90-second ad package, created by WPP Plc's J. Walter Thompson, Chicago, viewers will journey across America via the Wienermobile, seeing kids singing classic Oscar Mayer jingles.

Oscar Mayer has purchased two 10-second teasers during the first half promoting the half-time show, a 50-second commercial, "Wieners Across America," depicting highlights from the talent search contest that airs just before the half-time show. It also has a 20-second spot unveiling the talent search grand prize winner, three-year-old Andrew Thompson, from Nashville, Tenn., singing the Bologna Song.

Oscar Mayer hopes this year's Super Bowl will give the company the same kind of lift in sales as last year's game, which brought double-digit volume growth and significant share increases for its core brands: hot dogs, bologna and Claussen pickles.
"Our overall brand awareness jumped 50 percent during that time frame. It was hugely successful," Zander said.
